# crosswork_golden_config_templates (Resource)

This resource can manage a template of Golden Configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_golden_config_templates" "example" {
  name           = "cwtest-ntp"
  description    = "NTP servers"
  tags           = ["core"]
  vendor         = "Cisco Systems"
  software_type  = "IOS XR"
  product_series = ["Cisco XRv 9000 Series Virtual Routers"]
  config         = file("${path.module}/cwtest-ntp.j2")
  variables = [
    {
      name  = "ntp_server"
      value = "10.1.1.2"
    },
    {
      name             = "ntp_key"
      value_wo         = var.ntp_key
      value_wo_version = 1
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `config` (String) Configuration text with Jinja2 variables
- `name` (String) Template name, 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter
- `product_series` (Set of String) Product series of the devices; the controller does not check them against a device
- `software_type` (String) Software type of the devices, for example `IOS XR`
- `vendor` (String) Vendor of the devices, as the inventory spells it; the controller refuses a vendor the inventory does not know

### Optional

- `audit` (Boolean) Include the template in the global conformance schedule
  - Default value: `true`
- `config_type` (String) Format of the configuration text
  - Choices: `native`, `xml`, `json`, `c-style`, `j-style`
  - Default value: `native`
- `description` (String) Description, up to 255 characters
- `force_delete` (Boolean) Delete the template with force, which also removes it from devices it is applied to. Without it the controller refuses to delete an applied template.
  - Default value: `false`
- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.
- `mode` (String) How the configuration is applied: merged into the device or replacing what it covers
  - Choices: `merge`, `replace`
  - Default value: `merge`
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags of the template, up to 64 characters each
- `variables` (Attributes List) Variables of the template. Preferred over global variables. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables))

### Read-Only

- `config_id` (Number) The integer id of the configuration of the template, which a job refers to
- `id` (String) The id of the object
- `template_id` (Number) The integer id the controller gave the template

<a id="nestedatt--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variables`

Required:

- `name` (String) Variable name, 1 to 64 letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit

Optional:

- `type` (String) Type of the value
  - Choices: `STRING`, `JSON`
  - Default value: `STRING`
- `value` (String) Value; for the type `JSON` a JSON document, which the controller refuses to be empty
  - **Required**: exactly one of `value` and `value_wo` must be set.
  - This attribute stores the value in Terraform state. Use `value_wo` together with `value_wo_version` for a secret.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Value
  - **Required**: exactly one of `value` and `value_wo` must be set.
- `value_wo_version` (Number) Rotation trigger for `value_wo`. Increment this integer whenever the write-only value changes so Terraform sends the new value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import crosswork_golden_config_templates.example "<name>"
```
